items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Topics 61:1
items.html: The male of Atik is the level of Keter that came out in Atzilut on the screen of phase four, and the female of Atik is made of four aspects. The first is half of the Keter of Nekudim, which is the aspect of Katnut that came out in the Keter of Nekudim, considered only the aspect of the Guf and Etzem of Keter, since the lower vessels of Keter, which are AHP, came out only during Gadlut, and they are considered the lower half of Keter, which AA took. But Atik took only the upper half, which are the Guf and Etzem alone. The second is the GAR of Hochma, which is the aspect of Aba of Nekudim that came out during Katnut, likewise only of the aspect of the Guf and Etzem alone, since the ZAT of Hochma, which are the aspects of its AHP, were taken by Aba of Atzilut. The third is the GAR of Bina, meaning the aspect of the Guf and Etzem of Bina of Nekudim that came out during Katnut. However, this Guf and Etzem that came out during Katnut in the GAR of Nekudim in truth also includes Bina from the aspect of her own GAR, for although we say that AHP go outward, that does not mean the whole ten Sefirot of the ear, since the matter of going outward does not apply to the GAR of the ear, they being the light of Hassadim; rather, only the ZAT of the ear, which are already in an illumination of Hochma, went outward. Hence the Guf and Etzem that remained in Katnut also include the GAR of the ear. So the Guf and Etzem are considered the three Sefirot KHB. And all three aspects that the Nukva of Atik took from the GAR of Nekudim are the three aspects of GAR, namely GAR of Keter of Nekudim, GAR of Hochma of Nekudim, and GAR of Bina of Nekudim. However, Bina also took Hesed, and this is because as long as the ZAT of Bina had not yet expanded, Hesed was found included in Bina; hence it is considered that the Nukva of Atik took the four first ones of Bina, which are Galgalta, Einayim, GAR of the ear, and Hesed. The fourth is the Ketarim of ZAT of Nekudim, meaning from the aspect of what the Keter of Katnut illuminated to the ZAT of Nekudim, which the Nukva of Atik took as her own aspects of ZAT. And the reason the Nukva of Atik chose for herself all four of the aforesaid aspects is that she took all the lights that the breaking did not strike, and which are found in the place of her clothing, since the Rosh of Atik clothes the whole place where the GAR of Nekudim stood, as above in Answer 106. It follows on its own that she took all the lights that remained standing there. (Inner Light, page 625, Sub Header, “Atik”)
